### THE OPERATOR'S CALL: build a real PROJECT, three of them
The Cloud Master Projects shelf had nothing legitimate on it -- three projects registered, ZERO
built -- so someone filled it with the capstone LAB, and I then added a catalog entry that made
it render twice. Operator ruling: if it is a lab it cannot be a project. Fix = build real ones.

### PROJECT 1 "Build a Cloud Auditor" -- DESIGN COMPLETE, NOT BUILT
Student inherits an account wasting quota, builds a tool that finds orphans (volume attached to
nothing / security group on no server / network with no server / router with no interfaces --
all four confirmed VISIBLE to the grader; my first draft included snapshots, which the bridge
cannot see at all).
GRADING: the grader RUNS the student's tool. Mutate the tenant AFTER their last edit, exec their
program, compute ground truth server-side at that instant, pass on EXACT SET EQUALITY.
  Why not grade the report: Nancy killed v1 -- reading a findings file proves the REPORT is
  accurate, never that a TOOL produced it. A student can eyeball 15 resources and hand-type it.
  Why exact equality: containment lets a spray attack win (dump every id, 100% recall, zero
  classification), which makes Phase 2 optional.
  Why computed not seeded: the six labs leave ORGANIC orphans (quota forces server deletion,
  nothing tears down web-sg or lab5-net). Computed truth means a correct tool reporting them
  PASSES. Seeded truth would have failed my best students.
  Probes: created AND deleted per attempt (security_group quota is 10, measured -- create-only
  gave 9 attempts before exhaustion), matched by SERVER-RECORDED ID not name (else a student
  names a resource audit-probe-<their-session>-1 and hides a real orphan), session-scoped, with a
  grading lock carrying its OWN TTL so a hung exec cannot permanently lock a session.

### TOOLING MEASURED -- the numbers that decide the last fork
    CLI, 5 calls (5 processes)      19,363 ms      no new concepts   NON-VIABLE
    openstacksdk, ONE process        2,321 ms      auth free, library new     RECOMMENDED
    raw REST, ONE process              816 ms      teaches token auth from zero
    SDK x4 concurrent = 20 calls    10,184 ms  vs  CLI x4 = 4 calls at 24,303 ms  (~12x throughput)
#248 is CPU-bound, not memory (pinned at the cpus:0.5 cap; MEM peaked 61%, no OOM). The 4.8s is
process spawn + import, NOT API latency -- real round trip is ~130ms. So "raise memory" and
"raise cpus" both fix the wrong thing.
TWO FALSE READS CAUGHT BY CHECKING PAYLOAD, NOT THE CLOCK: a "50x win" that was 392ms of CRASHING
(credentials come from /etc/openstack/clouds.yaml, not env vars), and 404s from using the Keystone
CATALOG (returns bc2-internal addresses with no route -- clouds.yaml carries bridge overrides and
those must be used).
